testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You are braking on dry pavement at 55 mph. How much distance does brake lag add to your total stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: What happens if brakes become too hot?

options.text: The air compressor will kick in to cool the brakes

questions.explanation: If brakes overheat from too much use, they may stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: If you use spring brakes while hauling a heavy load, a complete stop will:

options.text: Take a short amount of time.

questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. When spring brakes activate because air pressure is low, your vehicle needs more distance to stop than normal. This is especially true when carrying a heavy load.

questions.question: An application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. This gauge helps drivers detect if their brakes are starting to fade.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should be no more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not exceed 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle should not be driven because something needs repair.

questions.question: Water and compressor oil are usually found in the compressed air of an air brake system. What should you do about them?

options.text: They are necessary for the air brake system to work properly.
Add more if the level is low.

questions.explanation: Water and compressor oil naturally collect in compressed air. If they build up, they can damage the brakes. You must open air tank drain valves daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: The most common type of foundation brake is the:
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps you maintain control during hard braking. However, it does not necessarily reduce your total stopping distance.

questions.question: To use the stab braking method, you should:

options.text: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll, then repeat.
Press the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock and the vehicle stops.
Use the emergency brake until the vehicle starts to slow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll, then repeat.
questions.explanation: The stab braking method means pressing the brakes all the way until they lock up. Then release the brakes until the wheels start rolling again. Repeat this process.

questions.question: Brakes can get out of adjustment quickly, especially:

options.text: If they are used a lot.

questions.explanation: Brakes lose adjustment quickly when they are hot. Check your brake adjustment regularly. For safe control, all brakes must work properly and be correctly adjusted.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.
Open the door to the cab.

questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Using both spring brakes and air pressure at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: While driving downhill, you should brake until your speed is:
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, brake until you reach 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: What can happen if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: If you press and release the brake pedal too often, air leaves the system faster than the compressor can replace it. If air pressure becomes too low, the brakes may stop working.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: There is a decreased risk of jackknifing.
There is an increased risk of jackknifing.
The brakes will not work as effectively as they would without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a decreased risk of jackknifing.
questions.explanation: When only the tractor has ABS and the trailer does not, the risk of jackknifing is reduced. The driver can still maintain steering control.

questions.question: What do the two systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, neither system will work.

questions.question: The safety valve on the first air tank opens:

options.text: If there is too little pressure.
If there is too much pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is too much pressure.
questions.explanation: The safety valve on the first tank releases air if pressure gets too high. It is usually set to open at 150 psi. If the valve opens, the system has a problem that needs repair.

questions.question: The air compressor governor stops pumping air when pressure reaches:
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when the air tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Where are ABS malfunction lamps located on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.

questions.question: The maximum air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes is:
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: To get normal stopping power, drivers with a front brake limiting valve should:

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Leave it in the "normal" position. The "slippery" setting was meant to reduce front-wheel skid, but it has not been found to be effective.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not recommended on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: To use the stab braking method in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock. Release the brakes until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process.
Apply the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Press the brakes fully, lock the wheels, and hold the brake pedal down until the vehicle stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock. Release the brakes until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process.
questions.explanation: Stab braking means pressing the brakes fully until they lock. Then release them until the wheels start rolling. Repeat this process.

questions.question: While driving downhill, brake until you reach a speed ____ below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When going downhill, brake until you reach 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle is:
questions.explanation: For a triple combination vehicle, the maximum air loss during an applied leakage test is 6 psi in one minute.

questions.question: Brakes may get out of adjustment:
questions.explanation: Brakes can lose adjustment quickly when they overheat from heavy use. Check brake adjustment regularly.
